question: Should generic tool-progress intent become a supported public Plugin SDK contract for channel plugins?
rationale: The branch adds externally importable API rather than only repairing Slack internals, so maintainers must choose and own the permanent cross-plugin contract.

options.title: Sponsor the generic contract
options.body: Keep the generic marker and predicate, document their semantics and compatibility expectations, add focused SDK contract coverage, and require exact-head integration proof before merge.

options.title: Internalize the signal
options.body: Remove the public exports and surface-budget increase, then carry the progress signal through a bundled-only contract that external plugins cannot depend on.

options.title: Pause for broader design
options.body: Hold the PR until progress intent is designed consistently across multiple producers and channel transports.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the generic contract
recommendation.body: Keep the generic marker and predicate, document their semantics and compatibility expectations, add focused SDK contract coverage, and require exact-head integration proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Slack delivery behavior and the public plugin boundary, and steipete has recent review history around the central Slack send pipeline.
